title: Importing and Exporting Build Planner .build Files in Path of Exile 2
summary: How the in-game Path of Exile 2 Build Planner reads .build data files: what they contain, where to put them on each platform, how to import and open them, how to pick the right level/budget stage, and how to validate and fix a file that will not load.
description: A practical guide to Path of Exile 2 Build Planner .build files: import, export, platform paths, the in-game stage selector, the build-file validator, and version compatibility.
imageAlt: An in-game build planner view representing importable .build files in Path of Exile 2
prerequisites: Path of Exile 2 installed (PC or Steam recommended)
A .build file from a trusted build creator
Access to your Documents / game files folder
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team

items.title: What is a .build file?
body: A .build file is a DATA file that stores a build's passive tree, ascendancy, skills, gear notes, and planner stages. It is not an executable program, and the Build Planner does not calculate real DPS - it only guides your in-game choices.

items.title: Where do I put it?
body: On Windows, place the file in Documents\My Games\Path of Exile 2\BuildPlanner. On Linux via Steam/Proton, use the Proton prefix's equivalent path. If the folder does not exist, the game creates it the first time you save or export, or you can create it yourself.

items.title: How do I use it in game?
body: Open the Passive Skill Tree or Gemcutting menu (press P on PC by current default), then click the blue icon / dropdown in the top-left corner and select your imported build. A blue line draws the recommended passive path.

sections.title: What a .build file contains
paragraphs: A .build file is a JSON data file the Build Planner reads to draw a guided overlay inside the game. It stores the build author, a description, ascendancy, passive allocations, recommended skills and support gems, and inventory gear notes.

It is important to understand what it is NOT. A .build file is not an executable - you never run it, and your operating system should not open it as a program. The Build Planner is also not a damage simulator: it shows you which nodes, gems, and gear the build recommends, but it does not compute real DPS or compare builds numerically.
bullets: Contains: passive tree plan, ascendancy, skills, support gems, gear notes, and planner stages.
Does NOT contain: code that runs, macros, or a DPS calculator.
Treat every .build file as plain data - only download from trusted sources.

sections.title: Downloading safely
paragraphs: A .build file is plain data, not a program, so it cannot execute code on its own. That said, only download .build files from trusted creators and communities you recognise.
bullets: Download only from sources you trust; the file is data, never run it as a program.
Prefer build pages that embed an official Export Build Planner button over unverified mirrors.
If a site asks you to execute or 'run' the .build file, that is a red flag - close it.

steps.label: Download the .build file
body: Get the file from a trusted build creator. If the build ships multiple level or budget variants, download the one matching your character.

steps.label: Place it in the BuildPlanner folder
body: Move or save the file directly into Documents\My Games\Path of Exile 2\BuildPlanner (Windows) or the equivalent Proton path.

steps.label: Create the folder if missing
body: If the BuildPlanner folder does not exist, create it, or open the in-game planner and export once so the game creates it for you.

steps.label: Restart if the game was already open
body: The file watcher detects new files on launch or refresh. If the game was running, restart it or refresh so the build appears.

steps.label: Refresh and select
body: Open the planner in game and confirm the build shows in the dropdown before following it.

sections.title: Opening a build in game
paragraphs: Once the file is detected, open the Passive Skill Tree or Gemcutting menu. On PC the default key is P. A blue icon appears in the top-left corner of the planner screen.
bullets: Click the blue icon to open the build dropdown.
Select your imported build from the list.
A blue line draws the recommended passive allocation path; red and green lines indicate weapon set I and II links.
Gear notes appear when you hover the blue icon on each equipment slot.

sections.title: Choosing the right growth stage
sections.intro: A build may ship several Level / Budget files. Pick the one that matches your character's current stage.

rules.title: Use the early leveling variant
steps: Pick the Level / Budget file whose notes describe your current level range.
Follow its passive path and suggested gems for that stage.
Switch to the next variant as you level up.

rules.title: Use the mid-budget variant
steps: Open the variant tagged for your current gear budget.
Match the gear notes to what you can actually afford.

rules.title: Use the endgame / capstone variant
steps: Select the endgame file for the full planned tree and best-in-slot notes.
Confirm your character meets the level and gem requirements it lists.

defaultResult.title: Match the file to your character
steps: Read each variant's notes to find the level and budget range it targets.
Load the variant closest to your current character, then advance to the next as you progress.

sections.title: Reading passives, skills, and gear notes
paragraphs: After selecting a build, the planner overlays its guidance across several panels. The Passive Skill Tree shows the recommended allocation path. The Gemcutting tab lists the suggested skill gems and support gems. Gear slots display stat-priority notes when you hover the blue icon.
bullets: Passive tree: follow the blue line node by node; weapon-set colours show set I / II links.
Ascendancy: the plan marks the recommended ascendancy choices.
Skills: the Gemcutting tab shows required skill and support gems from your Uncut gems.
Gear notes: hover the blue icon on each slot to read recommended priorities.

sections.title: Editing and exporting your own file
paragraphs: You can edit and export your own build from inside the game. The exported .build file captures the passives, ascendancy, skills, gear notes, and planner stages you set up, so you can share it or reload it later.
bullets: You control your own exported file - it stores the plan you built, nothing executable.
The file does not store live character stats, currency, or a DPS calculation.
Re-export after major changes so your saved file stays current.

sections.title: Build file validator
sections.intro: Use this to work out why a file is not loading. The validator only checks the extension, filename, and basic structure - it never executes code.

controls.label: What is wrong with the file?

rules.title: Rename to a .build extension
steps: The file must end in .build. Rename it if it saved as .txt or .json.
It is data - never set it to open with a program as executable.

rules.title: Fix the folder location
steps: Confirm the file is in the BuildPlanner folder, not a subfolder.
Restart the game so the file watcher picks it up.
Verify you used the correct platform path.

rules.title: Re-download from a trusted source
steps: The file may be corrupted or from a mismatched patch - re-download it.
Confirm the build's patch matches your game version.

defaultResult.title: General fix
steps: Check the extension is .build, the folder is correct, and the game was restarted.
If it still fails, re-download a clean copy from a trusted creator.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Most import failures come from a handful of avoidable mistakes.
bullets: Wrong folder: the file must sit in BuildPlanner, not Downloads or a subfolder.
Wrong extension: it must be .build, not .txt or .json.
Game not refreshed: the file watcher only sees new files after launch or restart.
Outdated build: a file from an old patch may not match the current tree - verify its version.
Treating it as a program: a .build file is data; never 'run' it.

items.question: Is a .build file safe to open?
answer: Yes - it is a plain data file, not an executable. It cannot run code. Only download from trusted sources and never open it as a program.

items.question: Does the Build Planner calculate DPS?
answer: No. It overlays a recommended passive path, skill gems, and gear notes. It does not compute damage. Use a separate planner for DPS math.

items.question: Why is my file not showing up?
answer: Check three things: the extension is .build, the file is directly in the BuildPlanner folder (not a subfolder), and the game was restarted after you added it.

items.question: Can I use .build files on console?
answer: As of 0.5.0 (checkedAt 2026-08-02) consoles do not support .build codes. Use a PC or Steam client for Build Planner imports.

items.question: How do I pick the right variant of a build?
answer: Each build may ship multiple Level / Budget files. Choose the one whose notes match your character's level and gear, and advance to the next variant as you progress.
